extracted.intended_audience: general public, readers, donors, prospective fellows, and journalists interested in Inside Climate News
extracted.subtask_description: An organization's 'About Us' page describing mission, editorial policies, governance, funding, and programs for a nonprofit climate newsroom. Useful for understanding editorial standards, funding transparency, access/republishing rules, and fellowship opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: publish essential reporting, investigation, and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Founded in 2007, Inside Climate News is the oldest and largest dedicated climate newsroom in the nation. We are nonprofit and non-partisan and exist to publish essential reporting, investigation, and analysis about the biggest crisis facing our planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsroom 'watchdog[s] government, industry and advocates and hold[s] them accountable for their policies and actions.' It also states goals to 'counter misinformation, hold polluters responsible, expose environmental injustice and scrutinize solutions.' This frames what counts as core editorial work and priorities for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit and non-partisan status
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside Climate News is a 501(c)(3) public charity and is nonprofit and non-partisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization operates without a paywall and relies on grants and donations. The tax-exempt status and non-partisan claim set expectations about funding, mission orientation, and neutrality of reporting. The page also provides EIN (56-2451141) and former legal name for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and donor non-involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Donors who support our award-winning environmental journalism do not have any involvement in or access to our editorial process or decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial independence is emphasized as an explicit policy; governance by a Board of Directors and adherence to best practices of non-profit management are invoked to reinforce this independence. Related links include 'Editorial Independence' and 'Donor Transparency' pages for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on environmental injustice and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Our newsroom maintains a focus on environmental injustice, consistently examining how climate change disproportionately burdens communities of color and vulnerable populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This editorial focus shapes story selection and prioritization. The organization also has a 'Justice Advisory Board' and includes Diversity, Equity & Inclusion as a named area, signaling institutional commitment to justice-oriented coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access / republishing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We make our work available without a paywall to ensure that anyone can read it, wherever they are. We also provide our stories to media partners for free to sustain the practice of environmental journalism, support local newsrooms and improve public understanding of science, health and the environment in communities across the nation, through ICN Local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to 'Republishing Guidelines' and 'ICN Local' for specifics; the stated policy is open distribution and free provision to media partners to maximize reach and support local outlets. This sets expectations for reuse and dissemination of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and training for emerging reporters (fellowship program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through our fellowship program, we provide hands-on newsroom experience for emerging reporters wanting to specialize in climate, environment and justice reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is presented as part of the organization's mission to cultivate new journalists in the field; relevant for prospective applicants and for understanding staffing/training priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and best practices of non-profit management
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside Climate News is governed by a Board of Directors and guided by the best practices of non-profit management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governance statement supports claims of accountability and institutional structure; links to 'Board of Directors' and 'Justice Advisory Board' provide more detail on oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial stewardship and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent audit of our 2019 fiscal year determined that 84 percent of our budget was used for program-related expenses: to pay staff and contributors to report, write, illustrate and edit articles; for travel; and for web development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references 'Funders', 'Annual Reports', and 'Financials' links. The stated audit result and breakdown are presented as evidence of financial stewardship and priorities; this informs donor/trustworthiness evaluations.
